archetypes.name: scope-drift
archetypes.rationale: The plan lists a drift-sweep step that names docs/issue-anchored-plan.md and other files not present in the files-to-modify section; a reviewer that cross-matches every file named anywhere in the plan body against the explicit update list will catch that gap.
archetypes.prompt_body: Cross-reference every file path mentioned anywhere in the plan body — including prose steps, drift-sweep lists, and inline examples — against the explicit 'Files to modify/create' section. Flag any file named in a step or sweep that does not appear in the file list, and any file in the list that has no corresponding prose update. Pay special attention to Step 6's drift-sweep targets (e.g. docs/issue-anchored-plan.md) versus what the file list actually enumerates. Also check whether every harness update the plan describes (assert_thin_fence calls, fat-pin removals, new pin additions) has a matching entry in the test files listed under scope-files. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: emit-contract
archetypes.rationale: The entire two-fence split design (--preview-only live vs --no-preview captured) rests on the claim that larch_quiet_init inside a command substitution duplicates FD 3 into the substitution pipe, so emit output from the captured driver is buffered; the plan must be verified against the actual emit/larch_quiet_init implementation to confirm this contract holds and the FD routing is correctly modeled.
archetypes.prompt_body: Locate and read the larch_quiet_init and emit/emit_kv implementations (likely in scripts/lib-quiet.sh or a sourced library), then verify the plan's key mechanic — that FD-3 output from emit inside a command substitution is buffered rather than live — matches actual behavior. Check whether --preview-only's live stdout path and --no-preview's captured KV stream are consistent with how larch_quiet_init sets up FD 3, and whether the LARCH_QUIET_DISABLE=1 test-mode path (emit routes to FD 1) interacts correctly with the capture logic described in the edge-cases section. Also verify that the plan's stdout-fallback 12-key allowlist parse order (later-terminal-KV-wins when no safe env loaded) is mechanically sound given the emit_kv call sites in run-step3-review.sh. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
